public_rationale: The passage quotes a summer 2025 essay, so it is assessed for June to August 2025. Marcus's example is illegal chess moves. On day 1 (5 August 2025) of the Kaggle Game Arena chess exhibition, Chess.com reported that Kimi k2 forfeited four games by failing to find a legal move. It said the Gemini 2.5 Pro vs. Claude 4 Opus match was the only one that day with more games ending in checkmate than in illegal-move forfeits. The same report named three key LLM weaknesses in chess: seeing the whole board, understanding how pieces interact, and making legal moves. PC Gamer (16 June 2025) reported an informal test in which ChatGPT 4o repeatedly lost track of where pieces were while playing Atari Video Chess. Chess.com said Grok 4 had not shown these limitations on day 1, so the weakness did not appear in every model. Reading 'stable' as reliable tracking of state, this evidence meets the support condition. It does not show leading models tracking board state reliably.
limitations: 'Stable models of the world' is a loose term. The result depends on reading it as reliable state tracking.
The evidence covers one tournament day and one informal test, both in chess. Other kinds of world modeling were not measured.
Grok 4 did not show these weaknesses on day 1. The evidence does not show how it did later in the tournament.
The evidence does not address whether LLMs have any internal world representation at all.
The ICML 2025 paper studies models trained for specific domains, not chat LLMs, so it is context only.
The 'number of limbs' example was not checked.

evidence.excerpt: The Gemini 2.5 Pro vs. Claude 4 Opus match was the only one to have more games finishing by checkmate than by illegal move forfeits.
evidence.explanation: In a tournament of eight leading LLMs, most first-round matches had more games lost to illegal moves than to checkmate. This matches Marcus's own example of failing to stick to legal moves.

evidence.excerpt: So far, LLMs have displayed three key weaknesses when it comes to playing chess: visualizing the entire board, understanding how pieces interact with each other, and making legal moves
evidence.explanation: The tournament report names board-state tracking and legal moves as general LLM weaknesses in August 2025.

evidence.excerpt: ChatGPT confused rooks for bishops, missed pawn forks, and repeatedly lost track of where pieces were—first blaming the Atari icons as too abstract to recognize, then faring no better even after switching to standard chess notation.
evidence.explanation: This is an informal but documented June 2025 test. In it, ChatGPT 4o repeatedly lost track of the board state.

evidence.excerpt: For now, Grok 4 has shown that it doesn't share the same limitations.
evidence.explanation: At least one model avoided these failures on day 1. This shows the weakness was not universal across all leading models.

evidence.excerpt: So far, foundation models are not capable of making the transition humans are capable of making: from good predictions to accurate world models.
evidence.explanation: This peer-reviewed finding says foundation models tend to learn task heuristics rather than world models. It is context only, because it studies models trained on specific domains, not chat LLMs.
